claim: TRIM5 proteins are restriction factors that block retroviral infections by binding viral capsids and preventing reverse transcription.
source: TRIM5 proteins are restriction factors that block retroviral infections by binding viral capsids and preventing reverse transcription.
evidence: This is a statement of established knowledge about TRIM5 proteins, supported by the broader scientific literature.

claim: Capsid recognition is mediated by C-terminal domains on TRIM5α (SPRY) or TRIMCyp (cyclophilin A), which interact weakly with capsids.
source: Capsid recognition is mediated by C-terminal domains on TRIM5α (SPRY) or TRIMCyp (cyclophilin A), which interact weakly with capsids.
evidence: This statement is supported by references to prior work and is consistent with established knowledge in the field.

claim: Efficient capsid recognition requires the conserved N-terminal tripartite motifs (TRIM), which mediate oligomerization and create avidity effects.
source: Efficient capsid recognition also requires the conserved N-terminal tripartite motifs (TRIM), which mediate oligomerization and create avidity effects.
evidence: This is a statement of established understanding about TRIM5 function.

claim: TRIM5 proteins assembled into hexagonal nets, both alone and on capsid surfaces.
source: Biochemical and EM analyses revealed that TRIM5 proteins assembled into hexagonal nets, both alone and on capsid surfaces.
evidence: This claim is supported by the biochemical and EM data presented in the manuscript.

claim: TRIM5 hexagonal nets comprise open hexameric rings, with the SPRY domains centered on the edges and the B-box and RING domains at the vertices.
source: These nets comprised open hexameric rings, with the SPRY domains centered on the edges and the B-box and RING domains at the vertices.
evidence: This structural description is based on EM analyses and subtomogram averaging presented in the manuscript.

claim: The principles of hexagonal TRIM5 assembly and capsid pattern recognition are conserved across primates.
source: Thus, the principles of hexagonal TRIM5 assembly and capsid pattern recognition are conserved across primates, allowing TRIM5 assemblies to maintain the conformational plasticity necessary to recognize divergent and pleomorphic retroviral capsids.
evidence: This conclusion is drawn from the observation that multiple primate TRIM5 proteins form similar hexagonal assemblies.

claim: TRIM5 assemblies maintain conformational plasticity necessary to recognize divergent and pleomorphic retroviral capsids.
source: Thus, the principles of hexagonal TRIM5 assembly and capsid pattern recognition are conserved across primates, allowing TRIM5 assemblies to maintain the conformational plasticity necessary to recognize divergent and pleomorphic retroviral capsids.
evidence: This is an interpretation based on the observed variability in TRIM5 lattice structure and its ability to bind diverse capsids.

claim: TRIM5α and TRIMCyp induce dissociation of retroviral core particles and inhibit reverse transcription.
source: TRIM5α and the related TRIMCyp protein (collectively TRIM5) are restriction factors that recognize the capsid surfaces of incoming retroviral core particles, induce their dissociation, and inhibit reverse transcription (Sayah et al., 2004; Stremlau et al., 2004; 2006).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior published work.

claim: The mechanistic basis for core inactivation by TRIM5 is not yet well established.
source: The mechanistic basis for core inactivation is not yet well established, but current models invoke the involvement of proteasomes (Anderson et al., 2006; Campbell et al., 2008; Diaz-Griffero et al., 2007; Kutluay et al., 2013; Lukic et al., 2011; Rold and Aiken, 2008; Wu et al., 2006), autophagosomes (Mandell et al., 2014a; 2014b), and/or the establishment of a general antiviral state (Pertel et al., 2011).
evidence: This is an acknowledgment of the current state of knowledge in the field, supported by citations.

claim: Current models for TRIM5-mediated core inactivation invoke the involvement of proteasomes.
source: The mechanistic basis for core inactivation is not yet well established, but current models invoke the involvement of proteasomes (Anderson et al., 2006; Campbell et al., 2008; Diaz-Griffero et al., 2007; Kutluay et al., 2013; Lukic et al., 2011; Rold and Aiken, 2008; Wu et al., 2006), autophagosomes (Mandell et al., 2014a; 2014b), and/or the establishment of a general antiviral state (Pertel et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Current models for TRIM5-mediated core inactivation invoke the involvement of autophagosomes.
source: The mechanistic basis for core inactivation is not yet well established, but current models invoke the involvement of proteasomes (Anderson et al., 2006; Campbell et al., 2008; Diaz-Griffero et al., 2007; Kutluay et al., 2013; Lukic et al., 2011; Rold and Aiken, 2008; Wu et al., 2006), autophagosomes (Mandell et al., 2014a; 2014b), and/or the establishment of a general antiviral state (Pertel et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Current models for TRIM5-mediated core inactivation invoke the establishment of a general antiviral state.
source: The mechanistic basis for core inactivation is not yet well established, but current models invoke the involvement of proteasomes (Anderson et al., 2006; Campbell et al., 2008; Diaz-Griffero et al., 2007; Kutluay et al., 2013; Lukic et al., 2011; Rold and Aiken, 2008; Wu et al., 2006), autophagosomes (Mandell et al., 2014a; 2014b), and/or the establishment of a general antiviral state (Pertel et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: TRIM5 proteins comprise a RING E3 ubiquitin ligase domain.
source: Like other members of the tripartite motif (TRIM) family (Reymond et al., 2001), TRIM5 proteins comprise a RING E3 ubiquitin (Ub) ligase domain (Meroni and Diez-Roux, 2005; Yamauchi et al., 2008), an L1 linker, a B-box 2 self-assembly domain (Diaz-Griffero et al., 2009; Javanbakht et al., 2005; Li and Sodroski, 2008), an antiparallel dimeric coiled-coil, and an L2 linker that folds back on the coiled-coil (Goldstone et al., 2014; Li et al., 2014; Sanchez et al., 2014; Weinert et al., 2015) (Figure 1A).
evidence: This structural description is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: TRIM5 proteins comprise a B-box 2 self-assembly domain.
source: Like other members of the tripartite motif (TRIM) family (Reymond et al., 2001), TRIM5 proteins comprise a RING E3 ubiquitin (Ub) ligase domain (Meroni and Diez-Roux, 2005; Yamauchi et al., 2008), an L1 linker, a B-box 2 self-assembly domain (Diaz-Griffero et al., 2009; Javanbakht et al., 2005; Li and Sodroski, 2008), an antiparallel dimeric coiled-coil, and an L2 linker that folds back on the coiled-coil (Goldstone et al., 2014; Li et al., 2014; Sanchez et al., 2014; Weinert et al., 2015) (Figure 1A).
evidence: This structural description is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: TRIM5 proteins comprise an antiparallel dimeric coiled-coil.
source: Like other members of the tripartite motif (TRIM) family (Reymond et al., 2001), TRIM5 proteins comprise a RING E3 ubiquitin (Ub) ligase domain (Meroni and Diez-Roux, 2005; Yamauchi et al., 2008), an L1 linker, a B-box 2 self-assembly domain (Diaz-Griffero et al., 2009; Javanbakht et al., 2005; Li and Sodroski, 2008), an antiparallel dimeric coiled-coil, and an L2 linker that folds back on the coiled-coil (Goldstone et al., 2014; Li et al., 2014; Sanchez et al., 2014; Weinert et al., 2015) (Figure 1A).
evidence: This structural description is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: TRIM5 proteins comprise an L2 linker that folds back on the coiled-coil.
source: Like other members of the tripartite motif (TRIM) family (Reymond et al., 2001), TRIM5 proteins comprise a RING E3 ubiquitin (Ub) ligase domain (Meroni and Diez-Roux, 2005; Yamauchi et al., 2008), an L1 linker, a B-box 2 self-assembly domain (Diaz-Griffero et al., 2009; Javanbakht et al., 2005; Li and Sodroski, 2008), an antiparallel dimeric coiled-coil, and an L2 linker that folds back on the coiled-coil (Goldstone et al., 2014; Li et al., 2014; Sanchez et al., 2014; Weinert et al., 2015) (Figure 1A).
evidence: This structural description is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: TRIM5α contains a B30.2/SPRY domain as its C-terminal viral core recognition domain.
source: TRIM5 proteins also contain one of two different C-terminal viral core recognition domains, a B30.2/SPRY domain in TRIM5α (hereafter termed SPRY) or a cyclophilin A (CypA) domain in TRIMCyp (Brennan et al., 2008; Newman et al., 2008; Nisole et al., 2004; Sayah et al., 2004; Stremlau et al., 2005; 2006; Virgen et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: TRIMCyp contains a cyclophilin A (CypA) domain as its C-terminal viral core recognition domain.
source: TRIM5 proteins also contain one of two different C-terminal viral core recognition domains, a B30.2/SPRY domain in TRIM5α (hereafter termed SPRY) or a cyclophilin A (CypA) domain in TRIMCyp (Brennan et al., 2008; Newman et al., 2008; Nisole et al., 2004; Sayah et al., 2004; Stremlau et al., 2005; 2006; Virgen et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: TRIM5 proteins act by binding the outer capsid shell of the viral core.
source: TRIM5 proteins act by binding the outer capsid shell of the viral core (Biris et al., 2013; Black and Aiken, 2010; Diaz-Griffero et al., 2006b; Kar et al., 2008; Kovalskyy and Ivanov, 2014; Langelier et al., 2008; Sayah et al., 2004; Sebastian and Luban, 2005; Stremlau et al., 2006; Zhao et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: The capsid protects and organizes the internal ribonucleocapsid, which comprises the viral NC protein, the RNA genome, and associated replicative enzymes.
source: The capsid protects and organizes the internal ribonucleocapsid, which comprises the viral NC protein, the RNA genome, and associated replicative enzymes.
evidence: This is a statement of established knowledge about retroviral capsid structure and function.

claim: Closed retroviral capsids are constructed from several hundred CA protein hexamers and exactly 12 CA pentamers.
source: Closed retroviral capsids are constructed from several hundred CA protein hexamers and exactly 12 CA pentamers ([Ganser et al., 1999; Gres et al., 2015; Li et al., 2000; Obal et al., 2015; Pornillos et al., 2011; Zhao et al., 2013] and reviewed in [Ganser-Pornillos et al., 2012; Zhang et al., 2015]).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work and reviews.

claim: Individual retroviral capsids are unique, asymmetric objects that can differ in hexamer numbers and pentamer distributions.
source: Although all retroviral capsids are organized following these principles, individual capsids are unique, asymmetric objects that can differ in hexamer numbers and pentamer distributions (Benjamin et al., 2005; Briggs et al., 2006; Butan et al., 2008; Ganser-Pornillos et al., 2004; Heymann et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: HIV-1 capsids are typically conical, but their sizes and cone angles can vary.
source: For example, HIV-1 capsids are typically conical, but their sizes and cone angles can vary, and cylindrical and spherical capsids also form (Benjamin et al., 2005; Briggs et al., 2006; Briggs et al., 2003; Ganser-Pornillos et al., 2004; Heymann et al., 2008; Welker et al., 2000).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Cylindrical and spherical HIV-1 capsids also form.
source: For example, HIV-1 capsids are typically conical, but their sizes and cone angles can vary, and cylindrical and spherical capsids also form (Benjamin et al., 2005; Briggs et al., 2006; Briggs et al., 2003; Ganser-Pornillos et al., 2004; Heymann et al., 2008; Welker et al., 2000).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Spherical and cylindrical capsids predominate in other retroviral genera.
source: Indeed, spherical and cylindrical capsids predominate in other retroviral genera, and capsid surface properties can vary considerably because CA proteins from different genera share low sequence identity (Berthet-Colominas et al., 1999; Campos-Olivas et al., 2000; Cornilescu et al., 2001; Ganser et al., 1999; Jin et al., 1999; Khorasanizadeh et al., 1999; Kingston et al., 2000; Momany et al., 1996; Mortuza et al., 2008; Mortuza et al., 2004; von Schwedler et al., 1998; Zlotnick et al., 1998).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: CA proteins from different retroviral genera share low sequence identity.
source: Indeed, spherical and cylindrical capsids predominate in other retroviral genera, and capsid surface properties can vary considerably because CA proteins from different genera share low sequence identity (Berthet-Colominas et al., 1999; Campos-Olivas et al., 2000; Cornilescu et al., 2001; Ganser et al., 1999; Jin et al., 1999; Khorasanizadeh et al., 1999; Kingston et al., 2000; Momany et al., 1996; Mortuza et al., 2008; Mortuza et al., 2004; von Schwedler et al., 1998; Zlotnick et al., 1998).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Individual TRIM5 proteins must overcome variations in retroviral capsid shape and sequence to function effectively.
source: To function effectively, individual TRIM5 proteins must overcome these variations in retroviral capsid shape and sequence (Hatziioannou et al., 2003; Wilson et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: TRIM5 proteins recognize pleomorphic capsids by recognizing repeating patterns on the capsid surface.
source: We, and others, have proposed that TRIM5 proteins recognize pleomorphic capsids by recognizing repeating patterns on the capsid surface (Biris et al., 2012; Ganser-Pornillos et al., 2011; Goldstone et al., 2014; Yang et al., 2012).
evidence: This is a model proposed by the authors and others, supported by citations.

claim: Flexible loops on the SPRY and CypA domains can adopt multiple different conformations and can bind weakly to conserved elements on the capsid surfaces.
source: This model supposes that flexible loops on the SPRY and CypA domains can adopt multiple different conformations and can bind weakly to conserved elements on the capsid surfaces (Biris et al., 2012; Caines et al., 2012; Kovalskyy and Ivanov, 2014; Price et al., 2009; Song et al., 2005a; Stremlau et al., 2005; Ylinen et al., 2010).
evidence: This is part of the pattern recognition model, supported by citations.

claim: Weak interactions between TRIM5 and capsid are amplified by TRIM5 assembly into a higher-order hexagonal lattice.
source: These weak interactions are then amplified by TRIM5 assembly into a higher-order hexagonal lattice, which positions arrays of SPRY/CypA domains to interact with repeating epitopes on the capsid surfaces (Ganser-Pornillos et al., 2011; Li and Sodroski, 2008).
evidence: This is part of the pattern recognition model, supported by citations.

claim: The pattern recognition model has been supported by biochemical and structural analyses of TRIM5-21R.
source: This 'pattern recognition' model has been supported by biochemical and structural analyses of a TRIM5 protein construct called TRIM5-21R, which is an artificial chimera in which the RING domain from human TRIM21 replaces the RING domain of rhesus TRIM5α (Diaz-Griffero et al., 2006a; Kar et al., 2008; Langelier et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: TRIM5-21R retains HIV-1 restriction activity.
source: The TRIM5-21R construct retains HIV-1 restriction activity, and has been used in several studies owing to its unusually favorable stability, solubility and assembly properties.
evidence: This is a statement about the properties of the TRIM5-21R construct.

claim: TRIM5-21R assembles into open hexagonal lattices, both alone and on the surface of 2D CA crystals.
source: Consistent with the pattern recognition model, TRIM5-21R was shown to assemble into open hexagonal lattices, both alone and on the surface of 2D CA crystals that mimic the surface of the HIV-1 capsid (Ganser-Pornillos et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior work.

claim: TRIM5-21R assemblies can be microns in size but lack strict long-range order.
source: TRIM5-21R assemblies could be microns in size but lacked strict long-range order, and 2D projections could therefore only be reconstructed to a resolution of ~7.5 nm.
evidence: This is a description of prior observations of TRIM5-21R assemblies.

claim: Domain positions in TRIM5-21R assemblies had to be inferred in the absence of high-resolution information on the structure of the TRIM5 protein core.
source: Domain positions therefore had to be inferred, and were interpreted in the absence of high-resolution information on the structure of the TRIM5 protein core.
evidence: This is a statement about the limitations of prior work.

claim: Technical challenges in purifying authentic HIV-1 cores have been a significant experimental limitation.
source: Technical challenges in purifying authentic HIV-1 cores have also been a significant experimental limitation, and all published biochemical and structural studies of TRIM5α-capsid interactions have therefore either employed crude viral core preparations or artificial mimics of the capsid surface (Black and Aiken, 2010; Ganser-Pornillos et al., 2011; Langelier et al., 2008; Sebastian and Luban, 2005; Stremlau et al., 2006; Zhao et al., 2011).
evidence: This is a statement about the state of the field, supported by citations.

claim: All published biochemical and structural studies of TRIM5α-capsid interactions have employed crude viral core preparations or artificial mimics of the capsid surface.
source: Technical challenges in purifying authentic HIV-1 cores have also been a significant experimental limitation, and all published biochemical and structural studies of TRIM5α-capsid interactions have therefore either employed crude viral core preparations or artificial mimics of the capsid surface (Black and Aiken, 2010; Ganser-Pornillos et al., 2011; Langelier et al., 2008; Sebastian and Luban, 2005; Stremlau et al., 2006; Zhao et al., 2011).
evidence: This is a statement about the state of the field, supported by citations.

claim: The interactions between authentic viral capsids and TRIM5 proteins have not been investigated biochemically or structurally prior to this study.
source: Thus, the interactions between authentic viral capsids and TRIM5 proteins have yet to be investigated biochemically or structurally.
evidence: This is a statement about the gap in knowledge that the current study addresses.

claim: Methods were developed for preparing authentic recombinant TRIM5 proteins, co-assemblies of TRIM5 and CA proteins, and stable HIV-1 cores.
source: To address these different shortcomings, we have developed methods for preparing authentic recombinant TRIM5 proteins, co-assemblies of TRIM5 and CA proteins, and stable HIV-1 cores.
evidence: This is a statement of the methods developed in the current study.

claim: TRIM5 proteins form hexagonal arrays on HIV-1 capsids.
source: These reagents were then used to demonstrate that TRIM5 proteins form hexagonal arrays on HIV-1 capsids.
evidence: This is a key finding of the study, supported by the data presented.

claim: Each hexagon edge in the TRIM5 lattice is ~19 nm long.
source: This model is attractive because the edges of each hexagon are ~19 nm long, which would accommodate the antiparallel TRIM5α coiled-coil (~17 nm), and the RING and B-box 2 domains would associate at the three-fold vertices, which is consistent with the trimeric B-box 2 domain structure presented in the accompanying paper (Wagner et al., 2016).
evidence: This is based on measurements from EM data and structural modeling.

claim: The antiparallel TRIM5α coiled-coil is ~17 nm long.
source: This model is attractive because the edges of each hexagon are ~19 nm long, which would accommodate the antiparallel TRIM5α coiled-coil (~17 nm), and the RING and B-box 2 domains would associate at the three-fold vertices, which is consistent with the trimeric B-box 2 domain structure presented in the accompanying paper (Wagner et al., 2016).
evidence: This is based on structural data.

claim: The RING and B-box 2 domains associate at the three-fold vertices of the TRIM5 hexagonal lattice.
source: This model is attractive because the edges of each hexagon are ~19 nm long, which would accommodate the antiparallel TRIM5α coiled-coil (~17 nm), and the RING and B-box 2 domains would associate at the three-fold vertices, which is consistent with the trimeric B-box 2 domain structure presented in the accompanying paper (Wagner et al., 2016).
evidence: This is based on structural modeling and is consistent with the trimeric B-box 2 domain structure.

claim: The L2 linkers fold back and form a four-helix bundle at the center of the coiled-coil.
source: Finally, the L2 linkers fold back and form a four-helix bundle at the center of the coiled-coil, and this platform could, in principle, buttress and orient the TRIM5α SPRY domains.
evidence: This is based on structural data and modeling.

claim: The L2 linker platform could buttress and orient the TRIM5α SPRY domains.
source: Finally, the L2 linkers fold back and form a four-helix bundle at the center of the coiled-coil, and this platform could, in principle, buttress and orient the TRIM5α SPRY domains.
evidence: This is a speculative statement based on structural modeling.

claim: Electron cryotomograms (ECT) were generated from tilt series of vitrified 2D crystals of full length TRIM5-21R and TRIM5-21RΔSPRY.
source: To visualize TRIM5-21R assemblies in three dimensions and define the SPRY domain positions, we generated electron cryotomograms (ECT) from tilt series of vitrified 2D crystals of both full length TRIM5-21R (Figure 1C) and a construct that lacked the SPRY domain (TRIM5-21RΔSPRY, residues 1–300, Figure 1D).
evidence: This describes the experimental approach used.

claim: TRIM5-21R and TRIM5-21RΔSPRY both assembled into similar planar lattices of hexagonal rings.
source: As expected, TRIM5-21R and TRIM5-21RΔSPRY both assembled into similar planar lattices of hexagonal rings, with inter-ring spacings and protein densities matching those of the previous 2D projection structures (Ganser-Pornillos et al., 2011).
evidence: This is based on ECT data and comparison to prior work.

claim: Difference density maps revealed that the SPRY domains are located at the center of each hexagon edge.
source: Difference density maps clearly revealed that the SPRY domains are located at the center of each hexagon edge (Figure 1E), thereby supporting the model shown in Figure 1B.
evidence: This is based on difference density analysis from ECT data shown in Figure 1E.

claim: The paracrystalline arrays of TRIM5-21R exhibited long-range order but diffracted poorly.
source: Although the paracrystalline arrays of TRIM5-21R exhibited long-range order, they diffracted poorly, suggesting variability within the lattice.
evidence: This is an observation from the EM data.

claim: Poor diffraction of TRIM5-21R arrays suggests variability within the lattice.
source: Although the paracrystalline arrays of TRIM5-21R exhibited long-range order, they diffracted poorly, suggesting variability within the lattice.
evidence: This is an inference from the diffraction data.

claim: The length distribution of hexamer edges in TRIM5-21R was centered about a mean of 19 nm, but individual lengths varied by up to ±5 nm.
source: The length distribution of hexamer edges was centered about a mean of 19 nm, but individual lengths varied by up to ±5 nm (Figure 1G, upper panel).
evidence: This is based on measurements from the ECT data shown in Figure 1G.

claim: The distribution of hexamer vertex angles in TRIM5-21R was centered about 120°, but varied by up to ±20°.
source: Similarly, the distribution of hexamer vertex angles was centered about 120°, but varied by up to ±20° (Figure 1G, lower panel).
evidence: This is based on measurements from the ECT data shown in Figure 1G.

claim: Individual rings within the TRIM5 lattice exhibit considerable conformational variability.
source: Thus, individual rings within the TRIM5 lattice exhibited considerable conformational variability, explaining the poor crystalline order and modest diffraction resolution.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the measurements of edge lengths and vertex angles.

claim: Conformational variability in TRIM5 lattice rings explains the poor crystalline order and modest diffraction resolution.
source: Thus, individual rings within the TRIM5 lattice exhibited considerable conformational variability, explaining the poor crystalline order and modest diffraction resolution.
evidence: This is an inference from the observed variability.

claim: Recombinant owl monkey TRIMCyp has been purified.
source: Recombinant owl monkey TRIMCyp has been purified (Pertel et al., 2011), but TRIM5α proteins are more challenging to purify because these proteins tend to self-assemble, both in cells and in vitro.
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior work.

claim: TRIM5α proteins are more challenging to purify than TRIMCyp because they tend to self-assemble, both in cells and in vitro.
source: Recombinant owl monkey TRIMCyp has been purified (Pertel et al., 2011), but TRIM5α proteins are more challenging to purify because these proteins tend to self-assemble, both in cells and in vitro.
evidence: This is a statement about the properties of TRIM5α proteins.

claim: Previous biochemical and structural studies of TRIM5α proteins have been performed with impure proteins, protein fragments, or non-native chimeric constructs.
source: Hence, previous biochemical and structural studies of TRIM5α proteins have been performed with impure proteins, protein fragments, or non-native chimeric constructs (Biris et al., 2012; Goldstone et al., 2014; Kar et al., 2008; Langelier et al., 2008; Sanchez et al., 2014; Yang et al., 2012; Ganser-Pornillos et al., 2011).
evidence: This is a statement about the state of the field, supported by citations.

claim: TRIM5 proteins were expressed in insect cells using a baculoviral expression system.
source: The strategy that was ultimately successful entailed expressing TRIM5 proteins in insect cells using a baculoviral expression system.
evidence: This describes the expression method used in the study.

claim: Expressed TRIM5 proteins formed cytoplasmic bodies that could be solubilized by lysing the cells in a low ionic strength, alkali buffer containing Triton X-100 and NDSB-256.
source: As described in greater detail in the Materials and methods, expressed TRIM5 proteins formed cytoplasmic bodies that could be solubilized by lysing the cells in a low ionic strength, alkali buffer that contained the non-ionic detergent Triton X-100, as well as a non-detergent small molecule, sulfobetaine-256 (NDSB-256) that has previously been shown to inhibit protein aggregation (Sainsbury et al., 2008; Vuillard et al., 1995).
evidence: This describes the purification method developed in the study.

claim: NDSB-256 has been shown to inhibit protein aggregation.
source: As described in greater detail in the Materials and methods, expressed TRIM5 proteins formed cytoplasmic bodies that could be solubilized by lysing the cells in a low ionic strength, alkali buffer that contained the non-ionic detergent Triton X-100, as well as a non-detergent small molecule, sulfobetaine-256 (NDSB-256) that has previously been shown to inhibit protein aggregation (Sainsbury et al., 2008; Vuillard et al., 1995).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Once solubilized, primate TRIM5 proteins typically remained dimeric and soluble under low salt, alkaline conditions in the absence of Triton X-100 and NDSB-256.
source: Once solubilized, primate TRIM5 proteins typically remained dimeric and soluble under low salt, alkaline conditions in the absence of Triton X-100 and NDSB-256, even at concentrations greater than 1 mg/ml.
evidence: This is an observation from the purification experiments.

claim: Primate TRIM5 proteins could be purified provided they were maintained at high pH, low salt and/or low protein concentrations.
source: The proteins could therefore be purified, provided they were maintained at high pH, low salt and/or low protein concentrations.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the purification experiments.

claim: Yields of purified TRIM5 proteins ranged between 1.3 and 9.6 mg/L of insect cell cultures.
source: Yields ranged between 1.3 and 9.6 mg/L of insect cell cultures, and all of the proteins eluted with similar retention times during the final gel filtration chromatography step, indicating that they were all dimers of similar shape.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the purification experiments.

claim: All purified TRIM5 proteins eluted with similar retention times during gel filtration chromatography, indicating that they were all dimers of similar shape.
source: Yields ranged between 1.3 and 9.6 mg/L of insect cell cultures, and all of the proteins eluted with similar retention times during the final gel filtration chromatography step, indicating that they were all dimers of similar shape.
evidence: This is an inference from the gel filtration data.

claim: All TRIM5 proteins except TRIMCyp could be purified to >95% purity.
source: All of the proteins could be purified to >95% purity (Figure 2B) with the exception of TRIMCyp, where our preparations also contained breakdown contaminants that mapped to proteolytic cleavage at residues Lys283 and Gln287 (not shown).
evidence: This is based on the SDS-PAGE analysis shown in Figure 2B.

claim: TRIMCyp preparations contained breakdown contaminants that mapped to proteolytic cleavage at residues Lys283 and Gln287.
source: All of the proteins could be purified to >95% purity (Figure 2B) with the exception of TRIMCyp, where our preparations also contained breakdown contaminants that mapped to proteolytic cleavage at residues Lys283 and Gln287 (not shown).
evidence: This is based on mass spectrometry analysis of the breakdown products.

claim: TRIMCyp breakdown contaminants were eliminated by creating a mutant construct TRIMCypK283D,Q287D.
source: These breakdown contaminants were eliminated by creating a mutant construct that expressed TRIMCypK283D,Q287D (Figure 2B, lane 4).
evidence: This is based on the SDS-PAGE analysis shown in Figure 2B.

claim: TRIMCypK283D,Q287D retains potent HIV-1 restriction activity.
source: These mutations are not expected to affect functionally relevant properties of the protein because TRIMCypK283D,Q287D retains potent HIV-1 restriction activity (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is based on the restriction assay data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: TRIM5αAGMpyg assembled into hexagonal arrays.
source: These screens identified conditions under which two of the TRIM5 proteins, TRIM5αAGMpyg (Figure 2C) and TRIMCyp (Figure 2D) spontaneously formed 2D hexagonal assemblies that were similar in appearance to those formed by TRIM5-21R (Ganser-Pornillos et al., 2011).
evidence: This is based on the EM images shown in Figure 2C.

claim: TRIMCyp assembled into hexagonal arrays.
source: These screens identified conditions under which two of the TRIM5 proteins, TRIM5αAGMpyg (Figure 2C) and TRIMCyp (Figure 2D) spontaneously formed 2D hexagonal assemblies that were similar in appearance to those formed by TRIM5-21R (Ganser-Pornillos et al., 2011).
evidence: This is based on the EM images shown in Figure 2D.

claim: TRIM5αAGMpyg and TRIMCyp formed 2D hexagonal assemblies similar in appearance to those formed by TRIM5-21R.
source: These screens identified conditions under which two of the TRIM5 proteins, TRIM5αAGMpyg (Figure 2C) and TRIMCyp (Figure 2D) spontaneously formed 2D hexagonal assemblies that were similar in appearance to those formed by TRIM5-21R (Ganser-Pornillos et al., 2011).

source: TRIM5α nets on bona fide cores were irregular, but exhibited a similar distribution of hexamer edge lengths (20 ± 2 nm, n = 51) and vertex angles (120 ± 2°, n = 68) as CA/TRIM5 'co-assemblies' (Figure 7—figure supplement 3).

claim: Restriction susceptibility is dictated at the level of capsid recognition.

evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the study's findings, supported by citations.

evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the observation that multiple primate TRIM5 proteins form similar hexagonal assemblies.

claim: Each ring edge in the TRIM5 hexagonal lattice is formed by a TRIM5 dimer that displays two SPRY (or CypA) recognition domains at its center.
source: Our EM analyses, together with recent crystal structures of fragments of non-assembling TRIM5 proteins that span the core coiled-coil and L2 linker regions (Goldstone et al., 2014; Sanchez et al., 2014), indicate that each ring edge is formed by a TRIM5 dimer that displays two SPRY (or CypA) recognition domains at its center.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the EM analyses and crystal structures, supported by citations.

claim: Capsid binding and TRIM5 assembly are coupled processes that cooperate to promote the recognition of pleomorphic retroviral cores with high affinity and specificity.
source: Most importantly, we find that capsid binding and TRIM5 assembly are coupled processes that cooperate to promote the recognition of pleomorphic retroviral cores with high affinity and specificity.
evidence: This is a key conclusion drawn from the study's findings.

claim: Hyperstable capsids may represent a useful starting point for the development of in vitro viral replication assays.
source: Hyperstable capsids may also represent a useful starting point for the development of in vitro viral replication assays, particularly if the capsid disulfides can be reduced without inactivating the internal reverse transcriptase and integrase enzymes.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about potential future applications.

claim: Recombinant TRIM5αrh proteins have been used successfully as antigens to generate monoclonal antibodies that can detect endogenous TRIM5α proteins.
source: For example, our recombinant TRIM5αrh proteins have already been used successfully as antigens to generate monoclonal antibodies that can detect endogenous TRIM5α proteins (NIH AIDS Reagent Program and (Imam et al., 2016).
evidence: This is a statement about the application of the purified proteins, supported by citation.

claim: There are indications that the different domains of TRIM5 work together as an integrated machine.
source: Moreover, although structural studies of TRIM5 protein domains and fragments have made valuable contributions to our understanding of TRIM5 structure and enzymology, there are a number of indications that the different domains work together as an integrated machine (Ganser-Pornillos et al., 2011; Goldstone et al., 2014; Li et al., 2013; Li and Sodroski, 2008; Reymond et al., 2001; Sanchez et al., 2014).
evidence: This is a statement about the importance of studying intact TRIM5 proteins, supported by citations.

claim: It will be important to study intact TRIM5 proteins, particularly to determine how capsid recognition is coupled to ubiquitin signaling.
source: It will therefore also be important to study intact TRIM5 proteins, particularly to determine how capsid recognition is coupled to ubiquitin signaling (Fletcher et al., 2015; Pertel et al., 2011; Yudina et al., 2015).
evidence: This is a statement about future research directions, supported by citations.

claim: Primate TRIM5 proteins accomplish the task of overcoming sequence and structural variability in retroviral capsids by coupling weak recognition of conserved capsid epitopes with hexagonal net assembly, thereby amplifying intrinsically weak binding affinities through avidity effects.
source: Primate TRIM5 proteins accomplish this task by coupling weak recognition of conserved capsid epitopes with hexagonal net assembly, thereby amplifying intrinsically weak binding affinities through avidity effects (Ganser-Pornillos et al., 2011; Price et al., 2009).
evidence: This is a summary of the pattern recognition model, supported by citations.

claim: The studies confirm that hexagonal net assembly is a conserved property of TRIM5 proteins.
source: Our studies confirm that hexagonal net assembly is a conserved property, but also reveal that the TRIM5 hexagonal nets are not highly regular.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the study's findings.

claim: The TRIM5 hexagonal nets are not highly regular.
source: Our studies confirm that hexagonal net assembly is a conserved property, but also reveal that the TRIM5 hexagonal nets are not highly regular.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the study's findings.

claim: The lack of strict regularity in the TRIM5 net may be required to adapt to the lack of regularity in the opposing retroviral capsids.
source: The lack of strict regularity in the TRIM5 net may be required to adapt to the lack of regularity in the opposing retroviral capsids, where every CA hexagon occupies a slightly different local environment and where pentagons and other kinds of lattice 'defects' are also prevalent (Byeon et al., 2009; Ganser-Pornillos et al., 2011; Gres et al., 2015; Hatziioannou et al., 2004; Obal et al., 2015; Pornillos et al., 2011; Yu et al., 2013; Zhao et al., 2013).
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the observed variability, supported by citations.

claim: Imaging studies have provided direct evidence that multiple TRIM5 molecules can bind continuously to incoming capsids.
source: Consistent with a lattice assembly model, imaging studies have provided direct evidence that multiple TRIM5 molecules can bind continuously to incoming capsids (Campbell et al., 2008; Danielson et al., 2012; Lukic et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: The stoichiometry of TRIM5-capsid interactions within cells is not yet known.
source: The stoichiometry of TRIM5-capsid interactions within cells is not yet known, but we find that TRIM5 molecules can cover most of the capsid surface in vitro.
evidence: This is a statement about the current state of knowledge.

claim: TRIM5 molecules can cover most of the capsid surface in vitro.
source: The stoichiometry of TRIM5-capsid interactions within cells is not yet known, but we find that TRIM5 molecules can cover most of the capsid surface in vitro.

claim: A patch of just 4–6 TRIM5 rings covers about half of the capsid surface.
source: A patch of just 4–6 TRIM5 rings covers about half of the capsid surface (see Figure 7), however, and would present ~40 recognition domains for avid capsid binding.
evidence: This is an estimate based on the structural data shown in Figure 7.

claim: A patch of 4–6 TRIM5 rings would present ~40 recognition domains for avid capsid binding.
source: A patch of just 4–6 TRIM5 rings covers about half of the capsid surface (see Figure 7), however, and would present ~40 recognition domains for avid capsid binding.

claim: The entire capsid probably does not need to be completely enveloped within a surrounding TRIM5 lattice for restriction to occur.
source: Thus, the entire capsid probably does not need to be completely enveloped within a surrounding TRIM5 lattice for restriction to occur.
evidence: This is an inference from the observation that a small patch of TRIM5 rings can provide substantial binding.

claim: CA mixing studies have shown that efficient TRIM5 restriction can occur even when only 25% of the capsid subunits are competent for TRIM5 binding.
source: Indeed, CA mixing studies have shown that efficient TRIM5 restriction can occur even when only 25% of the capsid subunits are competent for TRIM5 binding (Shi et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior work.

claim: TRIM5-mediated restriction appears to proceed via a multi-step pathway in which capsid recognition is followed by steps that lead to capsid dissociation and inhibition of reverse transcription.
source: TRIM5-mediated restriction appears to proceed via a multi-step pathway in which capsid recognition is followed by steps that lead to capsid dissociation and inhibition of reverse transcription (Pertel et al., 2011; Stremlau et al., 2006).
evidence: This is a statement about the mechanism of TRIM5 restriction, supported by citations.

claim: In cells, the later processes of TRIM5-mediated restriction can be decoupled from the initial binding event by treatment with proteasome inhibitors or by mutations in the RING domain.
source: In cells, the later processes can be decoupled from the initial binding event by treatment with proteasome inhibitors or by mutations in the RING domain (Anderson et al., 2006; Fletcher et al., 2015; Kutluay et al., 2013; Roa et al., 2012; Wu et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Proteasome inhibitors and RING domain mutations do not block TRIM5 binding, but presumably interfere with ubiquitin-mediated signaling events.
source: These treatments do not block TRIM5 binding, but presumably do interfere with ubiquitin-mediated signaling events.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the effects of proteasome inhibitors and RING domain mutations.

claim: TRIM5 binding can destabilize helical CA tubes in vitro.
source: Thus, although TRIM5 binding can destabilize helical CA tubes in vitro (Black and Aiken, 2010; Zhao et al., 2011), capsid dissociation and inhibition of reverse transcription appear to require ubiquitin-dependent signaling in cells (Campbell et al., 2015; Fletcher et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Capsid dissociation and inhibition of reverse transcription appear to require ubiquitin-dependent signaling in cells.
source: Thus, although TRIM5 binding can destabilize helical CA tubes in vitro (Black and Aiken, 2010; Zhao et al., 2011), capsid dissociation and inhibition of reverse transcription appear to require ubiquitin-dependent signaling in cells (Campbell et al., 2015; Fletcher et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Capsid binding can activate TRIM5 ubiquitin E3 ligase activity in vitro.
source: Capsid binding can activate TRIM5 ubiquitin E3 ligase activity in vitro (Pertel et al., 2011), and the structure of the hexagonal TRIM5 lattice suggests how this could occur.
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior work.

claim: The structure of the hexagonal TRIM5 lattice suggests how capsid binding could activate TRIM5 ubiquitin E3 ligase activity.
source: Capsid binding can activate TRIM5 ubiquitin E3 ligase activity in vitro (Pertel et al., 2011), and the structure of the hexagonal TRIM5 lattice suggests how this could occur.
evidence: This is an inference from the structural data.

source: Recent structural studies of the RING domains from TRIM37 (PDB ID: 3LRQ) and TRIM5α (PDB ID: 4TKP) (Yudina et al., 2015) have demonstrated that the RING domains function as dimers.
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior work.

source: However, the antiparallel structure of the TRIM5 coiled-coil precludes close contact of the two RING domains within a single TRIM5 dimer (Goldstone et al., 2014; Sanchez et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

evidence: This is based on the structural data shown in Figure 7D.

source: This idea is supported by 1) recent studies that demonstrate that autoubiquitylation occurs in vitro and in cells and that Lys45 and Lys50 within the RING domain of rhesus TRIM5α are preferentially ubiquitylated (Fletcher et al., 2015), and 2) the accompanying structural studies (Wagner et al., 2016) of a truncated rhesus TRIM5α protein comprising a B-box 2 and the truncated coiled-coil and L2 linker domains (termed 'mini-TRIM'), which reveal that the B-box 2 domains can mediate trimerization.
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: The accompanying structural studies reveal that the B-box 2 domains can mediate trimerization.
source: This idea is supported by 1) recent studies that demonstrate that autoubiquitylation occurs in vitro and in cells and that Lys45 and Lys50 within the RING domain of rhesus TRIM5α are preferentially ubiquitylated (Fletcher et al., 2015), and 2) the accompanying structural studies (Wagner et al., 2016) of a truncated rhesus TRIM5α protein comprising a B-box 2 and the truncated coiled-coil and L2 linker domains (termed 'mini-TRIM'), which reveal that the B-box 2 domains can mediate trimerization.
evidence: This is supported by citation to the accompanying paper.
